newsitem.title: USA: Rorer surges on buyout news.
newsitem.headline: Rorer surges on buyout news.

text.p: Shares in Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc surged in U.S. trading Thursday on news that Rhone-Poulenc SA plans a $4.3 billion bid for the stake in the U.S. drug company it does not already own.
Analysts said the deal made sense and speculated that the $92 a share that Rhone-Poulenc said it would pay for the remaining 31.7 percent Rorer stake could be a starting point for a higher bid.
"I think the deal will not get done at $92, that it will go higher, perhaps as high as $110 a share," said Rodman and Renshaw analyst James Keeney.
Keeney raised his rating on Rorer to buy from neutral.
American Depository Receipts in Rhone-Poulenc RP.N were sharply higher, up 6-7/8 to 43.
Rhone-Poulenc said it also plans to regroup its chemical and fiber operations into a single new unit, which would then be spun off and taken public in 1998.

This would allow Rhone-Poulenc to focus on its high-margin pharmaceutical business, which includes the Pasteur Merieux Connaught vaccines unit, and streamline administrative operations, analysts said.
The deal "would create a stronger health care company," said independent pharmaceutical industry analyst Hemant Shah. "That seems like the only purpose."
